chapter.name: Predicting What Comes Next: Exploring Sequences and Progressions
chapter.blurb: Sequences and their rules, arithmetic and geometric progressions, the sum of natural numbers, and fractal patterns.

scope_in.item: Sequences, terms, finite and infinite sequences, triangular and square numbers, the notation t_n
Explicit rule for the nth term; finding a term and testing whether a number is a term
Recursive rule for a sequence; the Virahanka-Fibonacci sequence
Arithmetic progressions: common difference, nth term, recursive rule, graph of an AP, applications
Sum of the first n natural numbers, sums of consecutive numbers and triangular numbers
Geometric progressions: common ratio, nth term, Sierpinski triangle and carpet, bouncing ball
End-of-chapter problems on APs and GPs

concepts.name: Sequences, terms and notation
concepts.description: A sequence as an ordered list of terms, finite and infinite sequences, the notation t_n, and triangular and square numbers.
concepts.idea: A sequence is an ordered list of numbers; the subscript in t_n tells the position of the term.
concepts.rule: Terms are t1, t2, t3, ... (or s_n, u_n). Triangular numbers 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, ... are sums of natural numbers up to that term. Square numbers 1, 4, 9, 16, ... are sums of the first n odd numbers.
concepts.example: For the odd numbers t1 = 1, t2 = 3, t3 = 5, t4 = 7.

concepts.name: The explicit rule for the nth term
concepts.description: Writing and using a formula in n for the nth term; finding a term directly and testing whether a number is a term of a sequence.
concepts.idea: An explicit rule gives any term directly from its position n, without needing the earlier terms.
concepts.rule: If t_n = f(n), then the 20th term is f(20). To test whether a number N is a term, solve f(n) = N; N is a term only if n is a natural number.
concepts.example: u_n = 2n - 1 gives the odd numbers; 137 is the 69th term because 2n - 1 = 137 gives n = 69.

questions.q: For t_n = n^2 - 2n + 3 find the first five terms and decide whether 27 is a term.

concepts.name: The recursive rule and the Virahanka-Fibonacci sequence
concepts.description: Defining a sequence by relating each term to earlier terms, including sequences using two or three previous terms.
concepts.idea: A recursive rule builds each term from earlier ones, so we must know the starting terms.
concepts.rule: t1 = 1, t_n = t_(n-1) + 3 gives 1, 4, 7, 10, ... . The Virahanka-Fibonacci sequence: V1 = 1, V2 = 2, V_n = V_(n-1) + V_(n-2), giving 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, ...

concepts.name: Arithmetic progressions
concepts.description: Sequences with a constant difference d, the nth term a + (n - 1)d, and using it to find terms and positions.
concepts.idea: In an arithmetic progression (AP) each term is obtained by adding the same number d to the previous term.
concepts.rule: AP: a, a + d, a + 2d, ... . t_n = a + (n - 1)d. Recursive rule t1 = a, t_n = t_(n-1) + d. The points (n, t_n) lie on a straight line.

concepts.name: Sum of the first n natural numbers
concepts.description: The formula S_n = n(n + 1)/2, the reversing method, sums of consecutive numbers and triangular numbers.
concepts.idea: Writing the sum forwards and backwards and adding gives n equal pairs.
concepts.rule: S_n = 1 + 2 + ... + n = n(n + 1)/2. The nth triangular number is n(n + 1)/2. The sum m + ... + k = S_k - S_(m-1).

concepts.name: Geometric progressions and fractal patterns
concepts.description: Sequences with a constant ratio r, the nth term a r^(n-1), and GPs arising from bouncing balls and the Sierpinski triangle.
concepts.idea: In a geometric progression (GP) each term is obtained by multiplying the previous term by the same number r.
concepts.rule: GP: a, ar, ar^2, ..., t_n = a r^(n-1). Recursive rule t1 = a, t_n = r t_(n-1). The points (n, t_n) do not lie on a straight line.
concepts.example: The number of black triangles in the Sierpinski triangle at stage n is 3^n; their area is (3/4)^n.

questions.q: In the Sierpinski triangle the number of black triangles grows fast but their area shrinks. Explain.
questions.a: Each stage multiplies the number of black triangles by 3, which grows quickly. But each stage multiplies the black area by 3/4, which is less than 1, so the area shrinks towards 0.
s: The count is multiplied by 3 each stage
The area is multiplied by 3/4 each stage so it decreases

The sum of the first three terms of a GP is 13/12 and their product is -1. Find the common ratio and the terms.
questions.a: Write the terms as a/r, a, ar. Their product is a^3 = -1, so a = -1. Then -1/r - 1 - r = 13/12, so r + 1/r = -25/12, giving 12r^2 + 25r + 12 = 0 and r = -3/4 or -4/3. The terms are 3/4, -1, 4/3 (or in the reverse order).
s: Middle term a = -1 from the product

questions.q: Ali says 1, -1, 1, -1, ... is not a GP because the signs keep changing. Evaluate.
questions.a: He is wrong. Each term is the previous term times -1, so it is a GP with common ratio -1.

questions.q: In the Sierpinski carpet, each stage keeps 8 of the 9 smaller squares. Write the number of red squares at stages 0 to 3 and at stage n, and the red area at stage n if stage 0 has area 1.
questions.a: Number of squares 1, 8, 64, 512, ..., which is 8^n. Each square has 1/9 of the previous area, so the area is (8/9)^n.
